definitions.explanation: An expression of sympathy offered to someone who has lost a loved one. The お prefix makes it polite. Used both as a noun and in set phrases when offering condolences.

examples.japanese: お{悔|く}やみを{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
{友人|ゆうじん}の{家族|かぞく}にお{悔|く}やみの{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote a letter of condolence to my friend's family.

examples.japanese: {突然|とつぜん}の{訃報|ふほう}に{接|せっ}し、{心|こころ}よりお{悔|く}やみを{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.english: Upon receiving the sudden news of the passing, I offer my heartfelt condolences.

notes:
FORMALITY:
お{悔|く}やみ is inherently polite due to the お prefix. The most common set phrase is お{悔|く}やみを{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます, a formal expression used at funerals and in writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{悔|く}やみを{申|もう}し{上|あ}げる (to offer condolences — formal)
- お{悔|く}やみの{言葉|ことば} (words of condolence)
- お{悔|く}やみの{手紙|てがみ} (condolence letter)
- お{悔|く}やみを{述|の}べる (to express condolences)
